hypothesis_tested: Assignment hypothesis: 'App shell chrome (TitleBar/TabBar/StatusLine) re-rendering unmemoized on every keystroke via shared Zustand store' is the remaining bottleneck after Stage 2's viewport-windowing fix.

measurement_method.instrument: Temporary render-probe (apps/tui/src/util/render-probe.ts, since REMOVED) — a no-op-unless-env-var-set function appended to a side-channel log file (never stdout/stderr, which would corrupt the Ink terminal frame). Called at the top of App, TitleBar, TabBar, StatusLine, Panel, and BoardView render bodies, plus inside BoardView's `j` keybinding handler, gated behind APERANT_RENDER_PROBE_LOG env var.

single_isolated_keypress.note: App/TitleBar/TabBar/StatusLine were observed rendering ONLY during the unrelated 2-second setInterval(refreshTasks, 2000) polling tick in App.tsx, timestamp-correlated to prove it was not keypress-triggered.

sustained_15_key_burst.ratio: Exactly 1:1 between handler invocations and BoardView/Panel renders — zero excess/wasted re-renders observed anywhere.
sustained_15_key_burst.note: All 4 registered handler calls landed within a ~15ms window at the START of the ~348ms burst, then silence for the remaining ~333ms — consistent with keystrokes being dropped upstream of React, not React failing to keep up with re-renders.

direct_measurement_result.conclusion: The assignment's hypothesis is DISPROVEN by direct measurement. App shell chrome does not re-render per keystroke, with or without the fix — React's existing narrow Zustand selectors (individual field selectors, not `(s) => s`) and the fact that `sel` lives entirely inside BoardView's own component state already prevent any chrome re-render. There was nothing to memoize that was actually re-rendering.

mechanism_1_render_throttle.finding: Ink 5.2.1 (confirmed installed version) throttles its OWN terminal repaint to at most once per 32ms, independent of React reconciliation speed. This is a hard architectural ceiling of ~31.25fps for ANY Ink application, unrelated to app code quality.
mechanism_1_render_throttle.implication: 60fps (16.67ms/frame) is structurally unreachable in this Ink version via any component-level optimization (memoization, selector narrowing, virtualization) — the bottleneck is below the React layer.

mechanism_2_keypress_coalescing.finding_verified_live: Directly tested: `parseKeypress('j')` returns `{name: "j", sequence: "j", ...}` (correct). `parseKeypress('jjjj')` returns `{name: "", sequence: "jjjj", ...}` — an UNRECOGNIZED pattern, because Ink's parser expects one keypress worth of bytes per stdin `data` event, not a multi-character run.
mechanism_2_keypress_coalescing.propagation_to_app: use-input.js:67 sets `input = keypress.sequence` (= 'jjjj' in the multi-char case, since ctrl=false and it's not in nonAlphanumericKeys). apps/tui/src/hooks/useKeymap.ts's normalizeKey() (line 34-35, OUT OF SCOPE for this task — not one of the authorized files) returns 'jjjj' verbatim for a plain non-modifier key. `ref.current['jjjj']` is undefined (only 'j' is a registered binding), so the ENTIRE coalesced chunk is silently dropped — zero scroll steps, not partial credit.
mechanism_2_keypress_coalescing.why_this_happens_under_sustained_input: tuistory's `type` command (and any sufficiently fast real-user key-repeat) can write multiple 'j' bytes to the PTY faster than the Node process's stdin read-loop drains them under system/process scheduling load. The kernel PTY layer coalesces the pending bytes into ONE read()/data event, which Ink's architecture (one data event = one parsed keypress) cannot decompose.
mechanism_2_keypress_coalescing.implication: This is the primary driver of the measured drop rate (73-93% across all three stages) — not a rendering-performance problem, an input-handling design limitation in Ink's keypress parser.

root_cause_found_instead.scope_note: Both mechanisms live in node_modules/ink (a third-party dependency) and, for the dispatch step, apps/tui/src/hooks/useKeymap.ts (NOT one of the files this task's scope was extended to cover — the assignment named BoardView.tsx, TitleBar.tsx, TabBar.tsx, StatusLine.tsx, Panel.tsx, and narrowly-scoped App.tsx selectors only). Fixing either would require patching/vendoring/upgrading the Ink dependency or editing useKeymap.ts, both outside the authorized scope for this task.

fix_applied_stage3.description: Wrapped TitleBar, TabBar, and StatusLine in React.memo. Applied as a legitimate, correct hygiene improvement (their props — plain strings/objects — are referentially stable across unrelated App re-renders, e.g. the counts/profile polling tick), NOT because measurement showed them re-rendering per keystroke — it showed the opposite. Documented honestly in-code as measured-not-to-matter.

file_deliberately_NOT_changed.reason: Panel's `children` prop is a freshly-created JSX tree on every call from BoardView. React.memo's shallow prop comparison would never find `children` referentially equal across renders, so wrapping Panel in React.memo would be a no-op that LOOKS like an optimization but never actually skips a re-render. Applying it anyway would be a misleading, dishonest change. Documented in-code with the reasoning instead.

fix_applied_stage3.app_tsx_selectors: Already narrow (individual field selectors: `useAppStore((s) => s.view)`, `useAppStore((s) => s.themeName)`, etc. — not a broad `(s) => s` subscription). No change needed or made; confirmed correct as-is.

measurements_all_three_stages.note: All three stages already pass this specific sub-metric. Stage 2->3 change (6.0ms->6.0ms) is a wash, as predicted by the direct render-probe evidence.

measurements_all_three_stages.stage2_to_stage3_delta: 96.4ms -> 94.3ms = 2.2% difference, well within measurement noise (individual trial-to-trial variance was already ±10% in Stage 2's own 8 trials). NOT a real improvement — consistent with the direct render-probe evidence that chrome components were never the bottleneck.
measurements_all_three_stages.verdict_for_this_measurement: STILL FAIL, unchanged in substance from Stage 2. 94.3ms/step remains ~5.7x slower than the 16.67ms/60fps budget.

measurements_all_three_stages.conclusion: Consistent within noise across all three stages (53-67% range) — confirms the 20-task board was never affected by either fix, as expected: it was never large enough for windowing to shrink its render tree, and chrome was never re-rendering to begin with.
Unchanged across all three stages, as expected (independent of the app under test). Confirms the measured M2 changes/non-changes are real application-level effects, not instrument drift.

navigation_correctness_recheck.method: 200 sequential single keypresses from task 1, column headers recorded as they scrolled into view.
navigation_correctness_recheck.result: PASS — unchanged and correct after chrome memoization.

manual_behavior_regression_check.method: Live session drive: pressed '6' to open Settings, moved theme selection with 'j', persisted with return (theme changed default -> matrix, confirmed ACTIVE marker and persistence), pressed '1' to return to Board (confirmed new theme applied instantly across the view switch — the already-proven P6.1a criterion), pressed 'j' twice (confirmed selection advanced correctly, task 1 -> task 3), pressed 'H' (confirmed column move persisted and logged: '003-add- ai_review -> in_progress (persisted)' in AGENT STREAM).
manual_behavior_regression_check.result: PASS — theme switching, tab switching, board scroll, column moves, persistence, and AGENT STREAM logging all function identically to before the chrome React.memo change. No behavioral regression from either the render-probe removal or the memoization.

verdict_reasoning: The chrome-memoization fix was applied correctly and is a legitimate hygiene improvement, but it produced no measurable change (94.3ms vs 96.4ms — within noise) because the assignment's hypothesis was empirically false: direct render-probe measurement proved App/TitleBar/TabBar/StatusLine never re-render per keystroke, with or without React.memo. The real, source-verified bottleneck lives in node_modules/ink's own architecture: (1) a hard-coded 32ms render throttle that caps ANY Ink app below 60fps regardless of React-level optimization, and (2) a keypress parser that processes one raw stdin data event as one keypress, silently dropping entire multi-character chunks that the PTY coalesces under sustained rapid input — verified directly by calling parseKeypress('jjjj') and observing it return an unrecognized empty-name result. Both mechanisms are outside apps/tui/src/views/BoardView.tsx, the four named chrome components, Panel.tsx, and App.tsx's Zustand selectors (which were already confirmed narrow and correct) — the authorized scope for this task. Fixing them would require either patching/vendoring/upgrading the Ink dependency itself, or editing apps/tui/src/hooks/useKeymap.ts (not named in the authorized file list). Reported honestly as FAIL with the specific unreachable-within-scope reasoning, per instructions, rather than claiming the memo fix helped when measurement shows it did not.
